rationale: Allowing longer enrollment periods expands the availability of childcare for families needing extended care.
Allowing certain motorcycles and bicycles to proceed through red lights expands their freedom from traffic-control restrictions.
The bill further specifies statutory exemptions from taxation, indicating reduced tax obligations for covered entities.
Mandatory sensitivity training for law enforcement indicates an expansion of institutional anti-discrimination requirements.
Creating a state utility-deposit guarantee program increases public intervention in utility-market transactions.
Removing criminal-offense status and a specified penalty for transporting feral swine reduces punitive enforcement.
Authorizing 18-to-20-year-olds to serve alcohol expands their permitted employment activity.
Creating a new state-controlled alcohol license places the activity within an expanded licensing regime.
The bill requires public high schools to facilitate voluntary military aptitude testing, supporting military recruitment and preparedness.
A presumption of unlawful use of force under specified conditions would constrain self-defense protections.
The amendment limits political subdivision involvement in banking and removes special constitutional banking restrictions.
The constitutional amendment repeals an existing constitutional provision governing legislative senatorial-district apportionment.
The bill authorizes adults to home-brew limited amounts of beer, mead, cider, and wine for personal use.
The bill promotes employment for individuals with disabilities through state programs and services, indicating a public-provision approach.
The bill establishes a custody rule limiting consideration of military deployment, directing courts toward a stricter protection of military service-related family arrangements.
Limiting trap-related liability to public land narrows private-land liability exposure.
The bill removes a statutory prohibition on deputy sheriffs practicing law.
